subject.title: [Feature Request] Telegram Channel: Support Thread Binding for Subagent Sessions

question: Should explicit Telegram `sessions_spawn(thread:true, mode:"session")` create and bind a child forum topic for subagent sessions, or should Telegram keep current-conversation binding unless a narrower opt-in design is approved?
rationale: Current main supports Telegram binding through the core adapter path, but selecting child forum-topic placement changes user-visible routing and conflicts with the open request to avoid exposing internal sub-agent runs as Telegram threads.

options.title: Sponsor narrowed child-topic support
options.body: Repair or replace https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82023 so explicit subagent thread spawns can create child forum topics while normal Telegram placement stays current.

options.title: Keep current-conversation binding only
options.body: Document that Telegram binds explicit thread-bound subagent sessions to the current topic or conversation and does not create child topics by default.

options.title: Defer to threading policy design
options.body: Hold the Telegram-specific request behind https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/56307 so channel threading semantics are decided through a broader plugin policy seam.

recommendation.title: Sponsor narrowed child-topic support
recommendation.body: Repair or replace https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82023 so explicit subagent thread spawns can create child forum topics while normal Telegram placement stays current.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice sits on the core SessionBindingService direction introduced by the merged core thread-binding refactor.
